contributions.statement: Never perform an agent rename from language-server references alone; grep beat even a warmed LSP on multi-file renames because comments, strings and config are not semantic references and a cold server returned one reference until files were opened.
contributions.evidence: §6.7: 6 renames, pass@1 grep 1.00 vs LSP location-only 0.67 vs text-inline 0.83, with the mechanism shown. Python/TypeScript, tiny N, self-declared preliminary.

contributions.statement: Add semantic (LSP) reference lookup only where grep is noisy for the identifier; its F1 gain tracked the grep false-positive rate (0 on clean names, +0.245 on noisy ones), not the language.
contributions.evidence: §6.5 Fig. 6: requests +0.072, remeda +0.000, hono +0.245 dF1; monotonic within hono over 6 targets; pooled slope ~-0.49. No CIs.

reason: The grep-vs-LSP conditions are specific and relevant to whether to add jdtls via MCP, but the paper is self-declared preliminary with tiny N and an untested arm, so it stays a hypothesis to rerun on Java repos.
